title: Waste and environmental obligations
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may triage, refer, document or hand over work connected with suspected drug use, storage or manufacturing contamination. This lesson does not grant authority to enter, investigate, sample, decontaminate, transport, dispose of material or issue any clearance.
learningOutcomes: Identify debris and material that must not go into household bins.
Stop a removal that has no written handler arrangement.
Record the stop-work decision and the referral to a waste handler.

instruction.heading: Waste and environmental obligations
instruction.body: Debris from a former laboratory, contaminated materials and other drug-related waste are not ordinary household rubbish. A crew that plans to put unknown former-laboratory debris into residential bins has made an error that must be stopped. Waste is identified, packaged, transported and disposed of through handlers and destinations approved for that purpose, under the environmental and waste rules that apply where the work is done. Do not remove any waste until the handler has been engaged and has confirmed the arrangements in writing. Record the stop-work decision and the referral.

procedure: Stop any plan to put unknown debris into household bins.
Hold the material in place and keep it separate from general waste.
Identify the waste-handling authority for the place of work.
Engage an approved handler and obtain written arrangements.
Do not remove any waste until the arrangements are confirmed in writing.
Record the stop-work decision and the referral.

workedExamples.situation: A crew plans to put former-laboratory debris into residential bins on collection day.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the plan. The debris is not household waste. The crew holds it in place and an approved handler is engaged in writing before any removal.

workedExamples.situation: A contractor offers to take the debris in a private trailer for a fee.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Transport without written handler arrangements and an approved destination is not acceptable. The offer is declined and the referral recorded.

equipmentAndPpe: PPE for handling waste as set by the assessment.
Labelled containers as the approved handler specifies.

commonErrors.error: Putting former-laboratory debris into residential bins.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop and engage an approved handler.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a private trailer as transport.
commonErrors.prevention: Decline. Use only the approved handler with written arrangements.

commonErrors.error: Removing waste before arrangements are confirmed.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold the waste until the handler confirms in writing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Waste is handled only by approved handlers under the applicable environmental and waste rules. Completing this lesson gives no authority to remove or transport waste.
The rules that apply to drug-related waste in each state and territory must be confirmed with the relevant authority before removal.
The Victorian guidance on clinical waste describes collection by EPA-licensed companies. That is a Victorian rule and does not apply to drug-related debris by default.

qualityStandard: No waste leaves the site without a written handler arrangement.
Every stop-work decision is recorded with the referral.
summary: Former-laboratory debris is not household waste.
No removal before written handler arrangements.

knowledgeChecks.question: A crew wants to put former-laboratory debris into household bins. What is correct?
options: Use the bins, because they are collected.
Stop, hold the debris and engage an approved handler before any removal.
Use the bins for the lighter items only.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be confirmed before drug-related waste is removed?
options: A verbal promise from the contractor.
Written handler arrangements from an approved handler.

officialReferences.title: Testing and remediation of methylamphetamine and illicit drug residues
officialReferences.pageDate: Last reviewed 21-05-2026 (no published or updated date shown)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. Describes a best-practice sequence: preparation, screening and detailed sample testing, a remediation action plan, clean-up, validation testing, and sample, clean-up and validation reports. Aim: residue below levels posing a risk to health and below the relevant health investigation level for the drug. Recommends that the company validating contamination differs from the clean-up company. Says testing and remediation companies need the necessary competencies and ethical standards. The page does not mention a licence or insurance requirement. Publisher: WA Department of Health.

officialReferences.title: Clandestine drug laboratories and cleaning contamination
officialReferences.pageDate: Last reviewed 22-05-2026 (no published or updated date shown)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03, at this health.wa.gov.au address. Says manufacturing sites are the highest-risk type; occupants and the public should not enter or attempt cleaning themselves; use qualified environmental professionals, and a testing and validation company separate from the clean-up company; test, remediate where residues exceed health investigation levels, then re-test and validate; keep records; check home insurance before arranging cleaning; report suspected drug manufacturing to WA Police. Publisher: WA Department of Health. Western Australian guidance only.

officialReferences.title: Duties of a person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. The PCBU must protect workers and others so far as reasonably practicable; hazards are eliminated where possible and otherwise minimised; for certain hazards a hierarchy of control applies (the page does not list its levels); duties cannot be contracted out. The page does not cover trauma cleaning, waste or PPE rules. Publisher: Safe Work Australia. The state or territory regulator confirms the adopted law.

officialReferences.title: Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03, first 100,000 of 133,773 characters only. Read: section 2.2 (standard precautions apply to all people), section 3.1.2 recommendations 7 and 8 (sharps handled minimally, never recapped, bent or broken, disposed of at point of use in an approved container not filled past its maximum fill line), section 3.1.3 recommendation 12 (spill response with gloves and protective equipment, containment, absorbent removal, detergent cleaning). Healthcare-setting guidance, applied here by analogy. Publisher: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC).

officialReferences.title: Managing exposures to blood and body fluids or substances
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. First response: remove contaminated clothing, wash with soap and water, flush mucous membranes, rinse eyes gently, report immediately; remove from duty and carry out a risk assessment; medical evaluation with post-exposure prophylaxis where appropriate; document date, time, type and circumstances. Victorian guidance only. The page shows its last update as 2015.

officialReferences.title: Cleaning and waste disposal procedures for infection control
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. Three waste groups (general, clinical, pharmaceutical); clinical waste in biohazard bags shown as yellow; sharps into containers that meet the Australian and New Zealand standards named on the page; clinical and pharmaceutical waste collected by waste companies licensed by the EPA and taken to EPA-licensed facilities. Victorian guidance only.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a property, investigate it, collect or test any sample, carry out decontamination or remediation, transport or dispose of waste, or issue any clearance, certificate or statement that a property is free of contamination. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate, approval or authority. Investigation, sampling, remediation and clearance are restricted work for suitably qualified and, where required, licensed professionals acting under a written plan. Police, regulatory and other official authority may control a site, and their release must be obtained in writing where it applies. Owner, manager, tenant or insurer permission does not replace it. In every case, stop and refer if the authority, the hazard or the qualification is uncertain.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: the authority or written release is missing or unclear; the hazard is unknown; a suspected laboratory or manufacturing activity is evident; anyone may have been exposed; a sample, test or result has no documented plan or custody; the PPE has not been approved; a waste route is unlicensed; a party asks for a clearance, a zero-contamination statement or disclosure of personal information; or the applicable jurisdiction is unknown. Stopping is a correct professional decision. Record it, and restart only when the authority has confirmed the scope in writing.
